Shizuku needs to access local network. It is controlled by the network permission.

Some systems (such as MIUI) disallow apps to access the network when they are not visible, even if the app uses foreground service as standard. Please disable battery optimization features for Shizuku on such systems.

In addition, Shizuku can be started automatically on boot. If not, please check if your system or third-party tools have restricted Shizuku.

Your device manufacturer has restricted adb permissions and apps using Shizuku will not work properly.

Usually, this limitation can be lifted by adjusting some options in "Developer options". Please read the help for details on how to do this.

You may need to restart Shizuku for the operation to take effect.
The permission of adb is limited

It\'s highly possible that your device manufacturer limits the permission of adb.

There may be a solution for your system in this document.
Run commands through Shizuku in terminal apps you like
First, Export files to any where you want. You will find two files, %1$s and %2$s.

If there are files with the same name in the selected folder, they will be deleted.\n\nThe export function uses SAF (Storage Access Framework). It\'s reported that MIUI breaks the functions of SAF. If you are using MIUI, you may have to extract the file from Shizuku\'s apk or download from GitHub.
Then, use any text editor to open and edit %1$s.
For example, if you want to use Shizuku in %1$s, you should replace %2$s with %3$s (%4$s is the package name of %1$s).
Finally, move the files to somewhere where your terminal app can access, you will be able to use %1$s to run commands through Shizuku.
Some tips: grant execute permission to %1$s and add it to %2$s, you will able to use %1$s directly.

With %1$s, in any terminal app, you can connect to and interact with the shell runs by Shizuku.

Device Owner mode providing boot-persistent Shizuku privileges without Wi-Fi.
Dhizuku Device Owner is a permanent, reboot-proof privileged mode. Requires a one-time PC ADB command setup or direct write on Rooted devices.
This app currently has Android Device Owner privileges. Elevated permissions are retained permanently across reboots without requiring Wi-Fi or PC connection.
Android security policy prohibits enabling Device Owner directly from system settings; it must be authorized once via PC ADB.

Why did the App Store disappear?

1. Account removal side-effect: In a zero-account state, Google Play or brand app stores automatically hide their launcher icons.
2. OEM Enterprise Policy: ROMs like Xiaomi HyperOS, OPPO, or Samsung Knox may hide consumer app stores when Device Owner is detected.

How to restore:
• Method 1 (Recommended): Re-login to your account (Google/Mi/Samsung) in Settings -> Accounts. The store icon will reappear.
• Method 2: Tap the Restore App Stores button below to unhide automatically.
• Method 3: Run adb shell pm enable & unhide from your PC.
Standard Device Admin Only (Not Device Owner)

Only Standard Device Admin was granted in system settings. Android security forbids Shell execution for Device Admin. Please activate Device Owner via PC ADB or use ADB / Root Start on the Home screen.
Detected standard Device Admin only. Under Android security policy, standard Device Admin cannot execute Shell commands. Please configure Device Owner via PC ADB or use ADB/Root Start on Home.

Why Some Apps (e.g. TikTok) Lock at 60Hz?

Android and One UI have built-in compatibility policies that force video streaming apps (TikTok, etc.) to 60Hz. On Samsung devices, go to Developer Options, scroll to the bottom and enter \"More settings\", then enable \"Disable app compatibility policies\" to unlock full 120Hz.
